name: Alphabet
description: Alphabet is the holding company of Google. About 62 percent of its revenue is Google Search advertising, with YouTube ads, the Google Network of ad partner sites, and a subscriptions, platforms and devices line (YouTube and Google One subscriptions, Play store, Pixel) making up most of the rest of Google Services, which earns about 90 percent of the profit of the two profit-making segments. Google Cloud (cloud infrastructure, AI infrastructure and Workspace) is the fast-moving second engine: revenue grew 82 percent to $24.8B in Q2 2026 and its operating margin reached 36 percent. Other Bets (Waymo self-driving rides, Isomorphic Labs, quantum and life-sciences efforts) lose about $5B a year. A large share of costs sits at the Alphabet level, mostly technical infrastructure and AI research, and shows up as a loss of $5.8B in Q2 2026.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. It describes Google Search and YouTube but not the Cloud business, which by Q2 2026 was 21% of revenue and 22% of operating income before Alphabet-level costs.

hq.note: From general knowledge; the address was not re-read from the 10-K cover in this pass.

businessLines.name: Google Search & other
businessLines.how: Advertisers pay per click or impression on search results and Google properties (Maps, Play, Gmail); volume is driven by search queries and ad pricing.

businessLines.name: YouTube ads
businessLines.how: Advertisers pay for video ads shown before and during videos; YouTube shares part of the revenue with creators.

businessLines.name: Google Network
businessLines.how: Google places ads on third-party sites and apps and passes most of the fee to the publisher, keeping a cut. Subject to the US ad tech antitrust case.

businessLines.name: Google subscriptions, platforms and devices
businessLines.how: Monthly or annual subscriptions (YouTube Premium and TV, Google One), a cut of app and in-app sales on Google Play, and one-time sales of Pixel phones and other hardware.

businessLines.name: Google Services (total of the four lines above)

revenue.note: Sum of the four revenue lines above plus hedging losses of $172M; derived, not a reported total in the excerpt read

businessLines.revenueNote: Sum of the four revenue lines above plus hedging losses of $172M; derived, not a reported total in the excerpt read

operatingProfit.note: Share is of Services plus Cloud only, before Other Bets and Alphabet-level costs. Margin computed. Q2 2026: $39,544M on about $94,540M, about 41.8%

businessLines.name: Google Cloud
businessLines.how: Enterprises pay usage-based fees for computing, storage and AI model use on Google Cloud Platform, plus per-seat subscriptions for Workspace; large multi-year commitments are common.

revenue.note: Q2 2026: $24,768M, +82% year over year (20.7% of Q2 revenue)

businessLines.revenueNote: Q2 2026: $24,768M, +82% year over year (20.7% of Q2 revenue)

operatingProfit.note: Q2 2026: $8,814M vs $2.8B a year earlier; margin about 35.6% computed. Share is of Services plus Cloud only.

businessLines.name: Other Bets
businessLines.how: Early-stage ventures, mostly Waymo (paid autonomous ride-hailing in several cities) and Isomorphic Labs; revenue is small and the segment is a cash sink funded by Services.
businessLines.description: 10-K names Waymo, Isomorphic Labs, quantum computing and life-sciences efforts.

operatingProfit.note: Q2 2026: -$5,789M. Not a business; unallocated costs, mainly technical infrastructure and AI model development shared across segments.

brands.name: Google Search, Maps, Gmail, Chrome, Android, Play
brands.note: Consumer surfaces monetised through the Services lines above; no separate revenue disclosed.

brands.name: YouTube
brands.share: $46,016M ad revenue FY2025 (11.4% of total) plus part of the subscriptions line

brands.name: Waymo
brands.share: Inside Other Bets ($382M Q2 2026 revenue for all of Other Bets)
brands.note: Uber and Waymo are ending their exclusive arrangement in Austin and Atlanta; Waymo plans its own app there in January 2028 (CNBC, 2026-07-24).

whatsNext.text: US search antitrust case: Google appealed the December 2025 final judgment (Jan 2026) and the DOJ and state attorneys general cross-appealed (Feb 2026); a stay request was denied as premature
Ad tech case: Judge Brinkema's remedies order (unsealed Sept 2026) rejects breaking up AdX and DFP but requires interoperability, auction-data sharing and a six-year monitor
whatsNext.source: The Next Web / AdExchanger / Axios, Sept 2026

whatsNext.text: 2026 capital spending is being raised: Q2 2026 capex was $44.9B; a cut in the share price followed the capex hike on results day
